fold.recommended: Accordion bellows, collapsed diaphragm form: flat annular flanks printed parallel with a real gel gap, joined at outer and inner crest rings, axis vertical in the gel, nose on the bed, tail cap on top. Axial growth only, diameter kept. A length tether stops the growth.

params.print_time_h: 1.5 at 50 mm/s, 3.7 at 20 mm/s (0.64 L, bead 1.6 x 1.5 mm)

fold.why: It is the only listed fold that prints as closed stacked rings with real gel gaps, has no vertices, needs no stiff panels, and never gets wider than the D 280 bore. Silicone can take the hoop stretch at the inner crests that paper cannot (Demaine et al. 2011; Dias et al. 2012), so the bellows opens by bending plus a small stretch kept at 1.25, under the 1.38 limit. Growth anchored at the tail pushes the nose out with about 20 N at 1 kPa. It also matches the artist note of 28 Oct: plain folded silicone, no Kresling.

rejected: Yoshimura
Diamond facets with many vertices; flat folded tiers touch, so no gel gap; diameter does not grow; facets must stay near rigid (Yoshimura 1955).
Kresling
Twists while it deploys, so the baby screws through the canal; bistability needs stiff panels that strain, which soft silicone lacks; diameter fixed. Artist ruled it out on 28 Oct.
Waterbomb

Can grow in diameter (stent from a 13 mm tube to 25.4 mm, about 2x, Kuribayashi 2006) but needs stiff facets and 6 crease vertices; every vertex needs gel gaps on many sides; silicone facets bend and lose the mechanism.
Everting tube
Grows from the tip, so the stored tube and the capsule cannot sit in one closed printed body; keep it as a canal liner (push methods).
Gored bud (meridian pleats)
Would grow in diameter, but meridian length is capped by the bed (about 340 mm), which limits the deployed D to about 190 mm; more complex paths for little gain.
Origamizer tucks (Demaine, Tachi 2017)
Watertight, but tucks stack many layers with zero gap; made for paper, not printable in gel.
demaine: Parallel or concentric pleats have no vertex conditions (Kawasaki, Maekawa); simplest crease class (GFALOP).
Not wanted: flat means zero gap and fused flanks. Print near flat with a 3 mm gap.
Not needed: silicone flanks bend and stretch; it matters only for stiff panel patterns (Abel et al. 2016).
Closed concentric pleats cannot open isometrically: paper buckles into a saddle (Dias 2012) or needs extra creases (Demaine et al. 2011). Silicone stretches instead: limit the stretch with a tether.
The printed folded shape is the rest state, so venting refolds the baby without help (programmable folding, Hawkes et al. 2010).

belly_fold.recommended: Concentric elliptical pleats (closed curved creases, a curved crease bellows dome) around a small crown cap, rim clamped at the seam. One pleat family, no vertices, no pleat ends.

params.stop: tether net or skin going taut at 10 L, then gas compliance 1.6 L/kPa
params.web_model_now: 17.9 L and 73 mm: about 2x too much for the air the baby takes in

belly_fold.why: A dome must lengthen along every meridian to rise. Closed concentric pleats store length in all directions, have no ends at the fixed seam, and no vertices. In paper a closed curved pleat buckles into a saddle (Albers 1927-28; Dias 2012; Demaine et al. 2011); in printed silicone the small hoop stretch (about 7 % at the innermost pleat) lets it rise round, with a faint saddle wobble at most. The current straight transverse pleats store length only along x: the web model needs about 10 % stretch across, and each pleat must die out where it meets the seam.
rejected: Straight transverse pleats (current)
Store length along x only; rise needs about 10 % stretch across; pleat ends at the clamped seam concentrate strain.
Waterbomb dome (proposal A)
Works only with stiff panels (1 mm PC) and about 190 triangles; vertex seals in silicone are the weak point; more parts.
Kresling
Needs twist; a dome clamped on a fixed elliptical rim cannot twist.
Yoshimura
A cylinder pattern, not a dome; many vertices.
Radial or flasher pleats
Open in plane, so the dome spreads and flattens instead of rising.
Pleated hypar (straight concentric squares)
Does not exist with only its creases (Demaine et al. 2011); folds to a saddle, not a dome.
Origamizer
Exact target shape but tucks stack layers with no gap; a paper method.
demaine: Recommended family; Demaine sculptures use concentric circles and ellipses; Albers pleat twists to a saddle in paper (erikdemaine.org/curved/history).
Inextensible pleats need extra creases; silicone uses stretch instead, kept under 10 %.
Neither is needed: the skin is printed folded with gaps and opens by bending.
Printed rest state = folded belly, so venting returns the belly to folded without help.

docking.geometry: Female lead in on the mother band: 35 to 40 deg half angle, 30 mm deep, R 150 to R 125, so it captures 21 to 25 mm of offset.
